title: Petition from the Society for the Preservation of National Parks against Granting San Francisco the Hetch Hetchy Valley
credit: National Archives, Records of the U.S. Senate, Committee Papers of the Committee on Public Lands from the 63rd Congress, NAID 7268060.
alt_text: Letter of June 27, 1913 from the Society for the Preservation of National Parks, California Branch, to Hon. George E. Chamberlain, Senate Chamber, signed by John Muir and other leading preservationists, urging Congress to defeat the Raker Bill, which called for a dam to be built across the Hetch Hetchy Valley.
notes: Artifacts research 2026-10-20: 2 page images Society_for_the_Preservation_of_National_Parks_001.jpg (2613x3347) and _002.jpg (2612x3379), plus a PDF, at catalog.archives.gov/medialive/60/2680/7268060/content/arcmedia/legislative/gallery/. Rights from useRestriction.status in MUI-S-0070. Stop 6 (Martinez) / Hetch Hetchy.

title: Passport application of John Muir, Volume 995: May 1 to 6, 1903
credit: National Archives at College Park, General Records of the Department of State, Passport Applications, Volume 995: May 1 to 6, 1903, NAID 235846313 (images 0420 and 0421; image provided by Fold3).
alt_text: Images of the passport application of John Muir, Year of Birth: 1838, in Volume 995: May 1 to 6, 1903 of the Passport Applications, General Records of the Department of State.
notes: Artifacts research 2026-10-20: the two images named 'Name: John Muir; Age/Year of Birth: 1838' in this volume (objectIds 235846729 and 235846730; 0420.jpg 3308x6001, 0421.jpg 3360x5961). Rights from the volume's useRestriction.status in MUI-S-0072. Read by eye on 2026-10-20, NOT facts (no transcription exists): sworn at Martinez, County of Contra Costa, 28 April 1903, stamped Passport Bureau May 5 1903; born at Dunbar, Scotland, 21 April 1838; emigrated with his parents in March 1849, sailing from Glasgow in the ship 'Warren' on or about 2 March 1849; naturalized 28 April 1903 before the Superior Court of Contra Costa County; occupation botanist and geology. Needs a human transcription (or a Citizen Archivist transcription) to become facts; this is the Warren ship lead. Stops 1-2 (emigration) and 6 (Martinez).
